brief: The town's windows light UP as the sun rises, which is backwards. Measured at #94 with probes/dawn-lit.mjs: windowLit's early risers key on the dawn EDGE at sunUp+1.3..2.1 h, so lit panes RISE after sunrise - 5 at dawn to 11 at sunUp+0.5 in winter. #98's named fix is to re-key hRise to sunUp-0.8..+0.4, so panes are lit BEFORE first light and go out as the town wakes. Small, but it sits on the morning: the clock button's second tap lands at sunUp+0.5 (watch note), which makes this the hour a visitor is most likely to look at after touching anything.
successLooksLike: At sunUp+0.5 in winter the count of lit panes is FALLING, not rising. Print the HEAD and candidate curves across the year from probes/dawn-lit.mjs, and show the evening curve is unchanged.
avoid: Do not touch the evening half of windowLit - it is tuned and the LIT_PANES night composite from #61/#93 depends on it. Do not add a morning source; the morning's population is b107's and b108's territory, not this brief's. Remember the hour of the sun is solved at the ARRIVAL instant: fixed-point any sunUp read on sunAt(t) rather than a stale value.
